name: Kofin Sync Queue
overview: Typed change queue for the Kofin Kodi client
description: Companion plugin for plugin.video.kofin: records library and user-data changes as typed records (change reason, series/season parents), serves them with query-time Etags and an in-band retention cutoff, so offline Kodi boxes catch up with minimal traffic.

versions.changelog:
- The logo sits inside its tile instead of running to the edges: the mark now
  has a 600x600 transparent canvas around it, which is the margin Jellyfin's
  plugin cards assume the image brings with it.

- Built for Jellyfin 12.0 as well as 10.11, from one source tree: the release
  carries a zip per server line, each declaring its own targetAbi, and a
  server installs the newest one it can run.
- The plugin has a logo. The catalogue entry and the installed plugin's tile
  show the Kofin mark instead of a blank placeholder.

- The logo sits inside its tile instead of running to the edges: the mark now
  has a 600x600 transparent canvas around it, which is the margin Jellyfin's
  plugin cards assume the image brings with it.

- Built for Jellyfin 12.0 as well as 10.11, from one source tree: the release
  carries a zip per server line, each declaring its own targetAbi, and a
  server installs the newest one it can run.
- The plugin has a logo. The catalogue entry and the installed plugin's tile
  show the Kofin mark instead of a blank placeholder.

- Records carry the libraries they belong to, and the feed can be filtered
  to them, so a client no longer fetches changes from libraries it does not
  sync. Announced as "library-scope" in the Info response's Features list.
- Records left behind by a deleted library are reaped rather than served
  until the retention cutoff.
- Version numbers now track the Jellyfin ABI (10.11.x), so which server a
  build targets is readable from the version alone.
- Releases are built and drafted by CI, and announced to the Kontell
  repository on publish.
- The plugin catalogue shows these notes: meta.json carries the changelog
  the repository manifest has been serving empty until now.

name: SyncPlay v2
overview: SyncPlay protocol v2 served from a plugin
description: SyncPlay protocol v2: versioned state, snapshots, position beacons, adaptive tolerances, bounded group-waits and robust reconnects — serving stock v1 clients and v2 clients from one group registry, replacing the built-in SyncPlay while installed.

versions.changelog:
- An item deleted while it sits in a group's queue no longer breaks the group
- An item with no runtime - live TV, external content - no longer zeroes
  every seek and position report
- Queue entries the server cannot resolve, for clients that declare they can
  play them. Capability: ExternalContent
- A group holding such entries is invisible to clients that cannot play it

- A member the group gave up on is waited for again when it reports ready
- A member the group timed out on is no longer recorded as a spectator
- A v1 member no longer gets a snapshot it cannot read
- A spectator's choice survives its next report
- v2-only updates no longer reach a v1 socket
- A timed-out v2 member is rendezvoused instead of abandoned
- A member that cannot seek into position no longer holds the group up
- A v2 member joining a playing group no longer pauses anyone. Setting: HotJoin
- Protocol v2: versioned state, snapshots, position beacons, ping-scaled
  tolerances, bounded group-waits, 90s reconnect grace

- Three defects a real v1 client found in a mixed group, none of them
  reachable with v2 members alone. A v1 member whose corrections did not
  converge was rendezvoused and sent a StateSnapshot it cannot read:
  WaitingGroupState gated on the *group* being a v2-capable context,
  which is always true here, instead of on the member's own negotiated
  version - the wait-timeout sweep had always gated on both that and the
  HotJoin config, and this path is now brought into line. A member that
  asked not to be waited for had that choice silently reversed:
  IgnoreGroupWait carried both "the group gave up on you" and "you asked
  not to be waited for", so the next report cleared both - jellyfin-web
  sets IgnoreWait when local playback resumes, and the group went back to
  counting a member sitting minutes away. And SendWireUpdate had no
  protocol gate of its own, so a v2-only update could reach a v1 socket;
  it is gated centrally now rather than at each caller that remembered.
- The rendezvous now happens where the group actually gives up on a
  member: the 10s wait timeout. Live measurement showed the correction
  branch it was added to in 10.11.0.3 is never reached by the member it
  was written for - a transcoding client answers a group Seek with one
  correction at ~7s, the wait timeout fires at 10s, and its next report
  lands after the group has left Waiting, so a policy needing a second
  correction never fires. Timing out a v2 member now pushes it a
  snapshot and answers its next Ready with a private scheduled Unpause,
  instead of abandoning it where it stood. v1 members are unaffected.
- A member that cannot seek into position no longer holds the group up.
  A transcoded stream lands a seek on its segment boundary rather than
  where the group asked, so the correction was sent again and again -
  measured at four rounds and ~13s of the whole group stalled, after
  which the member played on adrift anyway. It is now handed to the
  hot-join path instead: the group carries on, the member reloads, and
  its Ready is answered with a private scheduled Unpause at the live
  position. Give up after a correction that closes the gap by less than
  250ms, or after three attempts. Needs the matching kofin client to
  land tightly - the client aims its reload ahead by however long
  loading takes.
- Hot join: a v2 member joining a Playing group no longer pauses anyone.
  The group keeps playing, the joiner is pushed a snapshot, loads at the
  live position and rendezvouses via a private scheduled Unpause - with
  the updated kofin client it arrives with initial-start tightness. v1
  joiners (web) keep the classic barrier. Config: HotJoin (default on).
  Conformance: 17/17 fast suite including the new hot_join scenario.
- M1: the full protocol v2 engine (vendored from integration/syncplay-phase1):
  versioned state, snapshots, position beacons, ping-scaled tolerances,
  buffering grace, group-wait deadline, 90s disconnect grace with
  per-version resync. Body-transparent ProtocolVersion negotiation on the
  stock Join/New routes, POST /SyncPlay/Hello capability probe, dedicated
  WebSocket time sync at /SyncPlay/TimeSync, enriched /SyncPlay/List.
  Conformance: 11/12 with the unmodified kit, 12/12 with transport
  discovery; mixed v1+v2 groups verified via the conformance kit (stock-web
  wire compatibility proven in the M0 deployment pass).
